verdict.rationale: Elastic documents user-created alert rules that evaluate conditions continuously and fire notifications to third-party systems. It also offers proactive synthetic monitoring and markets the 'nightshift AI SRE' that detects and investigates incidents on its own. Together these give background automation, but the evidence is thin on user-configurable autonomous workflows beyond alerting. Missing for 10: documented general-purpose automation or workflow builder, explicit recurring schedule configuration, detail on how users configure the AI SRE's autonomous actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: You can create a rule to send an alert when the log aggregation exceeds a threshold.
You can also extend your alerts with notifications via services or third-party incident management systems.
Elastic nightshift AI SRE detects and investigates incidents, delivering evidence-backed root cause.
Proactively simulate user journeys and API calls to test application availability and functionality.
